summary:
PHASE-ZERO is an environmental compensation and anomaly detection platform for Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) surface monitoring, built for the Dancing with the SARs challenge. InSAR measurements of dams, slopes, and urban areas are frequently masked by seasonal noise—thermal expansion, rainfall infiltration, reservoir water-level changes, and atmospheric delays—making it difficult to distinguish harmless environmental cycles from true structural failure.

PHASE-ZERO solves this by fusing multi-band SAR observations (NISAR L-band and Sentinel-1/OPERA/RCM C-band) with real-time NASA POWER meteorology, NASA AppEEARS MODIS land surface temperature, SWOT reservoir elevation, and SRTM/Copernicus digital elevation models. Using phase-to-displacement physics, non-parametric Mann-Kendall trend tests, and Sen’s Slope significance (

Validated against calibrated Brazilian case studies—including Itaipu, Gongo Soco, Maceió, and a retro-forensic Brumadinho (2018–2019) series—PHASE-ZERO turns raw orbital radar data into actionable early-warning diagnostics.
details:
What It Does & How It Works PHASE-ZERO is a full-stack geospatial diagnostics dashboard that deconvolves environmental signals from InSAR surface displacement time series:

  1. Radar & Granule Discovery: Queries the NASA Common Metadata Repository (CMR) for NISAR (NISAR_L2_GUNW_PROVISIONAL_V1, NISAR_L2_GUNW_BETA_V1) and Sentinel-1 (OPERA_L3_DISP-S1_V1, ARIA_S1_GUNW) granules, and supports authenticated NASA Earthdata Cloud / ASF DAAC streaming of remote HDF5 files using WebAssembly (h5wasm) to extract unwrapped phase/displacement and coherence matrices.
  2. Environmental Compensation: Fetches daily meteorological series from NASA POWER (TS, T2M, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, PRECTOTCORR, RH2M, PS) to model thermoelastic deformation, rainfall pore-pressure loading, and wet/hydrostatic tropospheric delays, alongside SWOT reservoir water-level hydrostatic loading.
  3. Statistical Trend & Thermal-Shock Screening: Applies the CSA SAR Tutorial interferometric formulation (d=−λ4πΔϕd = -\frac{\lambda}{4\pi}\Delta\phid=−4πλ​Δϕ), Mann-Kendall non-parametric trend testing, and Sen’s Slope estimator (p<0.05p < 0.05p<0.05) to separate noise from real acceleration. It also integrates NASA AppEEARS (MOD11A1.061 MODIS LST) and precipitation data to compute a monthly Thermo-Pluviometric Shock Index (ICTI_{\text{CT}}ICT​).
  4. Interactive 2D/3D Visualization: Reconstructs an 18×18 3D terrain grid from a 5×5 Open-Meteo Elevation (SRTM 30m / Copernicus) query using B-spline interpolation, displayed alongside interactive Leaflet / MapLibre GL satellite maps (Esri World Imagery & OpenStreetMap), regime badges, and .xlsx report exports.

Benefits & Intended Impact Tailings dams, mining slopes, and subsiding urban zones require continuous monitoring, yet false positives from seasonal weather obscure early precursors. PHASE-ZERO empowers geotechnical engineers, civil defense teams, and researchers to inspect any custom coordinate or calibrated scenario (Itaipu, Gongo Soco, Maceió, and Brumadinho B1 2018–2019) with transparent physical baselines, reducing alert fatigue and improving early-warning readiness.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Architecture: 100% TypeScript strict monorepo (npm workspaces) with a shared domain/validation package (@phase-zero/shared).
  • Backend: Node.js (≥20), Fastify, Zod, h5wasm (remote HDF5 parsing via WebAssembly), and proj4 (UTM coordinate projections).
  • Frontend: Next.js 14, React 18, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, MapLibre GL, and SheetJS (xlsx) for data export.
  • Testing & Quality: Vitest (unit tests + golden numerical parity tests within ±0.01 against our legacy Python v4.2 scientific engine), Playwright (E2E), ESLint, and GitHub Actions CI.

Creativity & Factors Considered Rather than treating InSAR displacement as a raw number, PHASE-ZERO treats the Earth’s surface as a coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical system. Key factors considered include wavelength differences between L-band (238.4 mm) and C-band (55.5 mm), Line-of-Sight (LOS) incidence geometry, cloud-native HDF5 streaming without heavy local GIS servers, and strict numerical reproducibility verified by golden parity tests.
